minutes.headline: Green Community Task Force heard consultants on grants, a landfill solar idea and LED streetlights; no votes were taken.
minutes.summary: The task force met with an MRPC representative about contract help for the annual report and competitive grant admin, then with the Select Board chair about solar on the former landfill and energy data from the new facilities director. A streetlight consultant described LED conversion, controls and maintenance, and the group discussed whether the grant covers audit and design services. A next meeting was tentatively aimed at the 19th, and the meeting adjourned.

budget_items.what_was_said: Admin costs can be written into the competitive grant application up to a capped share; MRPC would need a contract to assist with quarterly and final reports.
DOER provides a per-community amount for annual reports, which MRPC thought would roughly cover the cost of its help this year.
MRPC is applying for a three-year brownfields assessment grant and could use some for the Lunenburg landfill site.
The Select Board chair suggested using ARPA funds to build solar on the former dump, with returns going to a capital fund.
The consultant said current streetlight cost would drop substantially with LEDs plus maintenance, with a short payback.
The consultant charges a percentage of the project and a per-fixture audit fee.
figures_as_heard: seven to seven and a half percent

budget_items.what_was_said: Roughly the amount approved for the conversion was stated; the town manager said the grant covers only conversion costs.
A three-year maintenance contract would likely be under a threshold that allows informal procurement.
The group estimated consulting fees might need to be covered outside the grant; the town manager was unsure the budget could absorb it.
The town is responsible for the cost of moving lights when poles are replaced.

decisions.decision: The task force will likely use MRPC for annual report help rather than a grant, and will work with the town manager on a contract.
The Select Board chair will send proposed environmental policies to the task force for feedback after the October 3 meeting.
The consultant will send the Wareham RFP as a template.
The chair will try to schedule the next meeting for the 19th, pending checking with absent members.

A landfill solar project funded from ARPA money would be a spending decision residents could be asked to vote on, though only an idea at this meeting.
